evals.prompt: evals/files/shop に evals/files/add-coupon.patch を当てる変更を、俯瞰してレビューして。
evals.expected_output: A review that states the design (two ways in, one shared validator, migrations for existing databases) and shows that the coupon check is not carried through: the nightly import stores unknown coupon codes, and existing databases never get the coupon column.
expectations: States the design read from the code: orders come in through api.create_order and import_orders.import_csv, and both rely on validation.validate_order
Points out that the nightly import (import_orders.import_csv) accepts a coupon code the web rejects, so an unknown code is stored on an order
Ties this to where the check was put: in api.create_order instead of the shared validation.validate_order
Points out that the coupon column was added by editing migrations/001_init.sql, so a database created before the change never gets it and the INSERT fails there
For each problem, names the file or function and says under what condition it happens and what then happens
Does not present line-level style remarks or general improvements outside this change as defects

evals.prompt: Review the design of this change before I merge it: evals/files/limit-qty.patch, applied to evals/files/shop.
evals.expected_output: A short review that says the change is sound: the limit sits in the shared validator, so the web and the nightly import both get it, with a test and the README updated. No problems are invented.
expectations: Says the change is sound in design
Gives the reason: the limit is in validation.validate_order, which both api.create_order and import_orders.import_csv call
Does not report a defect in this change (at most notes something as unconfirmed or as outside the change)
The review is short, in proportion to a small change

evals.prompt: evals/files/count-views.patch（evals/files/shop への変更）、マージして大丈夫か設計の目で見てほしい。
evals.expected_output: A review that shows what the change does besides counting page views: listing products now counts a view for every product, runs one query and one commit per product, and two requests at once can lose a count.
expectations: Points out that list_products now counts a view for every product listed, which is not what the change sets out to do (a view is a product page being opened)
Points out that list_products now runs a query, an update and a commit per product instead of one query
Points out that get_product, which reads like a read, now writes and commits
Points out that the count is read and then written back, so two requests at once can lose a view (or marks this as an inferred risk rather than a confirmed problem)
Keeps what was confirmed apart from what is inferred from the code
Notes as sound that the views column is added by a new migration (002_views.sql) rather than by editing the first one, or at least does not report it as a problem
